# Customitin: start here

Customitin is a headless personalization SDK for React Native/Expo and React web. These alpha packages are locally distributed, not published. Contracts and profiles are v2; breaking changes from the earlier styled shell are intentional.

The developer owns every screen, tab, theme, control, chat interface and confirmation appearance. Installation adds a provider and reviewed bindings. It does not add navigation, a theme, an editor, an empty screen or an AI chat. A developer-owned empty surface is the recommended starting example. Users can compose approved existing components with compatible approved data inside that space.

Read [integration](integration.md) before changing SDK integration or the CLI. [Contracts](contracts.md) defines supported behavior; [maintenance](maintenance.md) defines ownership, identities and recovery. [Testing](testing.md) distinguishes automated checks from release validation. `customitin guide --topic <name>` prints these same guides from packed artifacts.

## Packages

| Package                    | Responsibility                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@customitin/core`         | v2 contracts, registration, profile validation/storage, preview/apply/undo, conversation and action controllers, bounded data plans/formulas/joins |
| `@customitin/react`        | Shared provider/hooks, host-only SurfaceRenderer, HTTP/query adapters, browser storage; no React Native dependency                                 |
| `@customitin/react-native` | Shared React APIs plus in-place native section integration and native storage/navigation adapter exports                                           |
| `@customitin/server`       | Authenticated planner, remote data and action handlers; developer-owned model, data and domain services                                            |
| `@customitin/cli`          | Development-time source discovery, reports, reviewed enablement, generated bindings, refresh/watch/doctor/removal                                  |

## Rules for integrations

- Discover at development time. Runtime imports perform no filesystem scans, source edits or network requests. Provider registration diagnostics compare declared capabilities with executable bindings.
- Separate discovery, compatibility, enablement and static verification. A type signature is not authorization, evidence of complete data, mutation semantics or provider independence.
- Approve a report digest with explicit exclusions. Refresh preserves enabled IDs; new candidates remain pending. Completeness annotations describe source semantics and do not grant access.
- Choose explicit surface IDs for every planning request. Whole-app customization is an explicit collection of approved surfaces. Missing operation/field/action permissions deny access.
- Keep executable adapters in host code and serializable metadata in matching client/server manifests. Never evaluate AI-generated JavaScript or SQL.
- Only transform complete datasets locally. Partial caches and pagination need an explicitly registered remote executor.
- Action proposals are separate from layout proposals. Applying a layout never executes an action. Mutations require host confirmation by default, and layout undo does not reverse domain changes.
- Keep account scope and host authentication aligned. Store plans and mappings, not records, action results or chat history. V1 bytes are retained for recovery.
- Preserve developer-owned config/overrides, stable IDs and generated ownership boundaries. Never overwrite drift to make a check pass.

## Examples

`npm run dev:web` runs the Vite workspace. `npm run dev:tasks` includes a developer-owned Workspace tab with different native styling and the same core contracts. Both examples explicitly use a deterministic planner for their listed prompts. The existing recipe/movie/task visual shell is now example code under `examples/shared/src/ui`; it is not an SDK export or the default installation experience.

Use `npm run check`, packed consumer checks and interaction tests after changes. Update these source guides and run `npm run docs:build`; builds copy them into each package's `dist/docs`. Device, accessibility, performance and live-model checks remain release gates even when automated checks pass.

# Headless integration

## Install and review

Packages remain local until separately published. In the SDK repository:

```sh
npm ci
npm run pack:local -- /tmp/customitin-packages
```

Use the exact installation commands printed by the pack command. Install the emitted core and React tarballs as runtime dependencies; native apps also install the native tarball. Install **both server and CLI tarballs as development dependencies**: the local CLI depends on the unpublished server package for its bounded response reader. Omitting the server tarball makes npm try to fetch it from the registry. Do not import server code or model credentials into the app. The authenticated planner runs on the backend. Do not prescribe or install a chart, table or styling library: reuse the host's choices.

For example, using the default artifact directory and current alpha version:

```sh
npm install /tmp/customitin-packages/customitin-core-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz /tmp/customitin-packages/customitin-react-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz
# Native only, after the shared runtime packages:
npm install /tmp/customitin-packages/customitin-react-native-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz
npm install --save-dev /tmp/customitin-packages/customitin-server-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz /tmp/customitin-packages/customitin-cli-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz
```

Use the consuming app's existing compatible React/framework versions; the native peer ranges are React Native `>=0.83.0 <0.84` and React `>=19.2.0 <20`. Vite solution configs are supported: discovery and doctor select the referenced project containing the app entrypoint and honor its inherited settings and aliases. If multiple projects include that entrypoint, correct their includes before installing. Doctor checks the selected app project; still run the host's full build to check tooling/other projects.

In the app:

```sh
npx --no-install customitin inspect
npx --no-install customitin inspect --json
npx --no-install customitin init --approve-report REVIEWED_DIGEST --exclude FILE_OR_ID --dry-run
npx --no-install customitin init --approve-report REVIEWED_DIGEST --exclude FILE_OR_ID --apply
npx --no-install customitin doctor --typecheck
```

Replace the digest/exclusion with actual report values; omit `--exclude` when none is needed. JSON contains `review.digest`, source locations, usage sites, compatibility evidence, exclusions and actionable diagnostics. An approval fails if the reviewed source or policy changes. Approval stores enabled stable capability IDs, preserving overrides. `--complete`, `--component`, `--screen` and `--route` remain explicit individual decisions. New discoveries on refresh are not implicitly enabled.

The default installer adds a provider and generated bindings only. It preserves the host's styling and navigation. It does not create an empty surface automatically. Select the region to customize and create its controls in host code. Recognized Vite, Expo and Metro development commands are wrapped to refresh registration during development. Production imports do not discover code. Other React frameworks use manual provider placement; SSR/request-scoped storage and client component boundaries are host responsibilities.

## Declare a space

Use `defineComponent`, `defineSource`, `defineSurface`, `defineRelation`, `defineAction` and `defineCapabilities` from core for manual integrations. For generated integrations, put additional surface/component/action/relation descriptors in `personalize/overrides.json`, then refresh. IDs in those descriptors refer to the stable IDs in the generated registry.

A surface explicitly declares its mode, allowed components, required nodes, and policy:

```ts
const surface = defineSurface({
  id: 'workspace',
  title: 'Workspace',
  mode: 'compose',
  defaultLayout: [],
  requiredNodeIds: [],
  allowedComponentIds: ['host-chart', 'host-table'],
  policy: {
    operations: ['layout', 'data', 'actions'],
    sourceFields: {
      activity: ['id', 'teamId', 'hours'],
      teams: ['id', 'name'],
    },
    actionIds: ['complete-activity'],
    maxNodes: 20,
  },
  provenance: {
    version: 1,
    status: 'developer-reviewed',
    evidence: 'Host configuration',
  },
});
```

Use actual registered IDs. Absence of a permission denies it. A whole-app experience passes an explicit list of approved surfaces to `useAssistant`. A local section stays attached to its screen; reusing it elsewhere requires a separate reusable component adapter.

## Render with the host's components

Customization applies to the host's UI generally: text, cards, forms, containers, controls and library components. Charts are one data-binding example. Use `compose` for approved components and child slots, `properties` for a fixed element's allowed scalar props, and `reorder` for existing keyed sections. These modes share preview, apply, persistence and undo.

A host adapter receives `values`, `data`, `events` and `children`. Map these to the existing component's public API. A chart/table can accept the same typed series input and use different sources through validated field mappings. Discovery supports compatible scalar-record and array props plus `children`; unusual providers, callbacks, generic types and complex object shapes need reviewed adapters. Installed third-party usage is inventoried without scanning the dependency tree.

For example, a host `ProgressMeter({ value }: { value: number })` can wrap an installed native slider while keeping its styling, provider requirements and event behavior in host code. Approve that wrapper and expose only the intended props. The SDK does not need a slider dependency or a slider-specific renderer. For interactive controls, retain their callbacks in keyed existing sections or supply explicit host event/action bindings; do not turn callbacks into serializable props. See `fixtures/native-pilot` for this library wrapper, nested panel content, a property-only heading and existing input/callback sections.

```tsx
const bindings = {
  sources: hostSources,
  components: {
    'host-chart': ({ values, data }: HostComponentProps) => (
      <ExistingChart
        title={String(values.title)}
        data={data?.series?.rows ?? []}
      />
    ),
  },
  actions: hostActions,
};

<CustomizationProvider
  options={{ registry, storage, scope, planner }}
  bindings={bindings}
>
  <YourExistingApplication />
</CustomizationProvider>;
```

This sketch requires the host's real types/exports. Strongly typed charts may need an explicit conversion from scalar rows; validate against their declared data input first. Keep component functions stable rather than declaring new component types inside renders.

In a host-owned screen, place `<SurfaceRenderer id="workspace" />`. It renders registered host components and containers only. Supply its `status` callback for loading, empty single-record, unavailable binding or render failures. It inserts no fallback text or visuals. For array inputs, the host component owns its empty-state appearance.

Use `useAssistant(['workspace'])` for request, cancel, preview, apply, undo, reset and conversation state. Render previews explicitly with `<SurfaceRenderer id="workspace" preview />`. Use `useSurface(id)` for approved nodes and manual preview commands; `useDataView(id, surfaceId)` for data/loading/more/refresh; `useAction(surfaceId, actionId)` for explicit proposals and execution. Display errors and disable controls during pending host writes. Hooks expose structured codes; choose your own user-facing wording.

See compiling examples in `examples/shared/src/headless` and `examples/web-app`. Their host controls centralize English copy and handle rejected saves. `examples/shared/src/ui` contains the earlier optional visual demo, now owned by the examples.

## Reuse an existing chart with another dataset

An exported chart taking `data: readonly ChartRow[]`, where `ChartRow` is an interface with `label: string` and `value: number`, can use a generated binding. Named interfaces, readonly arrays, memo and child slots are supported. Approve the chart and each source independently. For example, a complete hours loader might return `{ id, team, hours }` and a complete budget loader `{ id, department, budget }`. The chart's prop names need not match either source.

1. Review `inspect --json`; apply the reviewed digest, with any exclusions. Find the chart/source **stable IDs** in `personalize/capabilities.json`.
2. Add a `compose` surface to the existing overrides, as above. Allow the chart ID, `layout` and `data` operations, and the selected fields from both sources. Run `refresh --apply`. Keep `components[chartId].source` unset: it is a legacy single-source item restriction, not a chart dataset selection.
3. Render `SurfaceRenderer` and host controls using `useAssistant(['workspace'])`. Connect a planner through the developer-owned config. A planner proposal uses `setDataView` followed by `setSurfaceLayout` with these shapes (replace the placeholder IDs):

```ts
const view = {
  id: 'chart-data',
  title: 'Budget by department',
  plan: dataPlanSchema.parse({
    sourceId: budgetSourceId,
    project: ['department', 'budget'],
  }),
};
const node = {
  id: 'existing-chart',
  componentId: chartId,
  props: {},
  children: [],
  data: {
    data: {
      viewId: 'chart-data',
      mapping: { label: 'department', value: 'budget' },
    },
  },
};
```

Here `data` is the chart's actual prop name. Import `dataPlanSchema` from core. Wrap these values in the proposal's `setDataView`/`setSurfaceLayout` operations with `surfaceId: 'workspace'`, the current request ID, registry revision and base revision. To show hours, keep the same component ID, change the source and projection to `team`/`hours`, and map `{ label: 'team', value: 'hours' }`. No replacement chart or handwritten chart adapter is needed. Preview does not save; host controls call apply, cancel or undo separately.

The packed consumer runner implements this exact sequence in `fixtures/headless-interactions/planner.ts` and `interaction.tsx`, using the generated root and bindings in fresh native/Vite apps. Its planner is deterministic test support, not a natural-language service. Mismatched field types, denied fields and incomplete datasets remain errors; supply a reviewed host adapter for unsupported shapes.

## Existing screens and elements

`customitin init --screen 'src/screens/Home.tsx#Home' --apply` connects supported static keyed sections in place. The generated wrapper preserves the host's lexical scope, callbacks and provider context. No editor or style primitive substitution is inserted. Implement reorder/hide controls with `useSurface`; see the compiling/interaction fixtures in `tests/helpers/screen-consumer.ts`. Web uses `@customitin/react/dom`; native uses `@customitin/react-native`.

For a single element, register a `mode: 'properties'` surface whose default layout contains the host element. Grant `operations: ['properties']` and an `editableProps` allowlist. It may change only those props; identity, position, children, bindings and locked props remain fixed. The compiling property example is `examples/shared/src/headless/element.tsx`.

## Connect account, persistence and endpoints

Generated `personalize/config.ts` is developer-owned. Its optional `useHostConfiguration()` reads host context above the SDK provider and supplies reactive `scope`, `storage`, `planner`, `plannerContext` and `bindings`. `bindings.session` stays local and flows to data/action adapters. Changing scope/session rebuilds transient runtime state; do not use a shared local-device scope for authenticated datasets.

Vite setup uses a lazy browser storage adapter. Native setup reuses installed AsyncStorage, otherwise reports memory storage as unfinished setup. Provide encrypted storage when required by the host. Storage keys include app, schema version and account scope.

`plannerContext` is an explicit host callback returning up to 20 permitted scalar values (for example a selected record ID). Nothing reads source rows or action results into model context automatically. Treat model output as proposals; unresolved record references need clarification or host selection.

Deploy matching manifests with `createPlannerHandler`. For remote transformations, register a `RemoteDataAdapter` and optionally use `createDataHandler` on the authenticated backend. For domain actions, adapters call existing services; `createActionHandler` requires authentication, account/revision resolution and durable host idempotency. Client adapters may use existing networking clients; include the registry revision and surface ID in endpoint requests. The SDK does not supply backend domain logic, credentials or deployment.

Remote data adapters receive `context.appId`, `context.registryRevision` and `context.surfaceId` alongside the plan, optional cursor, cancellation signal and local session. Send `{ appId, registryRevision, surfaceId, plan, cursor }` to `createDataHandler`. Action handlers receive `context.appId` and the validated `context.proposal` alongside the idempotency key; send `{ appId, registryRevision: proposal.registryRevision, surfaceId: proposal.surfaceId, proposal }` to `createActionHandler`. Forward the signal to the host network client and supply host authentication. Session objects stay local; server handlers obtain account scope and current revision from their trusted host context adapter.

# Supported v2 contracts

## Discovery and registration

Discovery uses TypeScript at development time, follows reachable local workspace imports/aliases/re-exports, and recognizes supported callable wrapped components (including memo). It inventories named/default/namespace third-party JSX imports used by the app without scanning dependency trees. Traversal is bounded and excludes generated files, tests, dependency trees, native output and likely secrets.

Platform and routing are detected separately from imports and entrypoints. Vite/React and native/Expo have provider-only setup. Multiple routing systems produce a diagnostic rather than assuming one global navigator. Custom framework roots require manual placement. Discovery is static: it never executes host modules or infers provider independence, business authorization, mutation semantics or completeness from types.

Reports distinguish discovered candidates, bindable shapes, explicitly enabled IDs and doctor-verified static installation checks. Verification does not mean device or live-model verification. Unsupported unselected candidates do not prevent unrelated valid bindings. Required callback props identify the adapter needed; the SDK never invents event behavior. Scalar props, scalar-record inputs, arrays of scalar records and a React children slot are supported automatic component bindings. A required complex field inside a record/array needs a host wrapper. Explicit legacy `components[id].source` retains a source-restricted item adapter for old host-rendered collections.

Sources support bounded complete array loaders, exported repository methods, zero-argument TanStack Query option factories and explicit `@customitinQuery` query-page contracts. `@customitinComplete` describes semantics, not authorization. Query functions must operate on the complete dataset authorized for the current account. Cached rows alone do not establish completeness. Existing QueryClient and navigation-ref integration are retained when explicitly selected. Enabling a navigation binding adds no route or visual navigation.

## Headless rendering and surfaces

Metadata is serializable; executable component/source/action/remote adapters stay in host code. Core has no platform/UI dependency. Shared React imports have no React Native dependency. SDK packages export no shell, editor, theme palette, chat UI or styling primitives. Provider diagnostics report absent/mismatched bindings; a missing adapter affects its capability rather than adding fallback UI.

`compose` allows approved host nodes in a developer-chosen space. `reorder` preserves original local sections and permits only reordering/hiding. `properties` fixes structure and allows only listed scalar props. Per-surface policies grant operations, components, source fields, actions, optional explicit navigation/appearance bindings and maximum nodes. Missing permissions deny access. Client and server both validate target IDs, current profile revision, capability revision, component/data/event compatibility and references. A data view shared with a surface outside the request cannot be changed by that request. No planning target means rejection.

In-place integration supports 1–40 static direct keyed sections with a single unconditional return. Native containers are directly imported vertical View/ScrollView; web containers include main/div/section/article/aside. Stable keys, test IDs or unique tags supply identities. Conditional/mapped content belongs inside a stable keyed section. FlatList, horizontal/custom/sticky containers and ambiguous roots need host adapters. The wrapper retains hidden sections mounted to preserve local state and callbacks; hiding does not suspend subscriptions or grant authorization. Native wrappers can affect flex/focus geometry and need device checks. Host state persistence across an actual process restart remains the host's responsibility; SDK persistence restores the layout and section identities.

## Typed data plans

A data input declares named scalar fields, required/nullability rules and cardinality `one` or `many`. A binding maps those fields to a named data view's projected fields. Multiple compatible approved datasets can feed the same component. Mismatched types, required fields, source restrictions, nullable results or ambiguous automatic mappings are rejected or require a host adapter. Optional nonnullable fields omit null values before reaching the host; required values cannot disappear.

Plans contain a base source, projection, filter expression, sorting, computed fields, grouping and count/sum/average/min/max aggregates. Inner/left equality joins require an approved relation with compatible declared keys and cardinality. The initial implementation joins each relation from the base source; arbitrary chained relations and many-to-many relationships need a host remote adapter and a supported bounded plan. Undeclared relationships are rejected. Left-join missing values become null. Null join keys never match. Duplicate keys violate declared one-to-one/many-to-one relationships; row expansion remains bounded even for approved one-to-many joins.

Formulas are interpreted expression trees: `{literal}`, `{field}`, or `{op,args}`. Operators are add/subtract/multiply/divide, eq/lt/gt, and/or/not, if, concat, coalesce. There is no evaluation of code, property traversal, arbitrary function calls, SQL or model-selected network requests. Trees are limited to depth 8 and 100 nodes. Types are checked first. Arithmetic propagates null; division by zero returns null; nonfinite numbers are rejected. Ordered comparisons with null return false; equality is strict (including null equality). Boolean operators propagate null. A conditional takes its first branch only for true. Concatenation accepts strings; coalesce returns the first nonnull value. Text results are bounded to 500 characters. Numeric aggregates ignore null; empty sum/average/min/max return null, count returns zero.

Local execution requires every source descriptor and returned page to be complete with no next cursor, within source and result budgets. It never aggregates a partial cache. Default result/source budget is 10,000 rows; default operation budget is 100,000 and an explicit core executor limit cannot exceed 1,000,000. Joins, grouping, formula evaluation and sorting consume the budget. Cancellation is checked across loads and bounded processing. Result keys derive from source IDs, typed record keys and join/group identities; filtering/sorting do not reassign index identities.

Use `execution: 'remote'` only with an explicit `RemoteDataAdapter`. It must enforce server authorization, operate on full authorized datasets before pagination/aggregation and return projected validated rows, stable unique keys, completeness and a nonrepeating cursor. `createDataHandler` revalidates policies and output. A remote result may be paginated; the React hook merges pages by stable key with a bounded total. Action invalidation and source invalidation subscriptions reload dependent plans, including joined sources. Persistence stores plans/mappings only.

## Actions and assistant

An action declares typed arguments/results, `effect: 'read' | 'write'`, confirmation (required by default), and invalidated source IDs. `available` and `execute` adapters reuse authenticated host services. Component event descriptors map typed event values to action arguments through validated expressions. An event proposes an action; it never executes it implicitly. Chat returns a separate `action-proposal` response. The lifecycle is proposed → awaiting-confirmation → executing → succeeded/failed/cancelled.

Execution requires a separate host call. When confirmation is required, absence of a host callback blocks execution. An explicit `host-managed` descriptor delegates confirmation to the host. Both are deliberate developer policy decisions. Permission, arguments, surface, revision and account context are checked immediately before dispatch. Actions are blocked during layout preview/saving; new previews cannot start while an action is pending. Layout apply never runs an action, and layout undo does not reverse a business mutation.

Mutation handlers receive an idempotency key. Duplicate submissions in the active runtime are rejected; the bounded set fails closed after 1,000 submitted IDs. No automatic mutation retries occur. The host backend must authorize records and durably deduplicate across retries/restarts/instances. `createActionHandler` requires that durable adapter and trusted account/revision lookup; it does not treat the client's confirmation as backend authorization. Cancellation after dispatch cannot guarantee that a remote mutation did not occur. Report uncertain results and reconcile with the domain service before retrying.

Execution adapters receive explicit routing context: remote data gets app ID, capability revision and selected surface ID; actions get app ID and the validated action proposal. These values let host clients construct scoped endpoint requests without guessing from component state. Server handlers validate the request and supply their own authenticated account/session context to backend adapters.

Assistant context is bounded to 12 in-memory turns, supports clarification/cancel/preview/apply/undo/reset and clears on account changes. Conversation, rows and action results are not persisted. No rows/results are sent to the model automatically. Explicit host-permitted scalar context is optional; model text and permitted context are never authorization. Planning context is reduced to the requested surfaces and allowed metadata before invoking a server model provider.

## Profile compatibility

Registries and profiles declare schemaVersion 2. ProfileStore first reads v2 head/backup, then v1 recovery bytes if migration has not been retired. It reconciles compatible stable host identities; unsupported old shell/theme/destination settings produce warnings. V1 bytes are not overwritten or removed. Successful v2 writes/erasure retire automatic v1 fallback so deleted profiles do not reappear. Save/export recovery bytes before any separate host retention/deletion operation. Old histories that cannot validate are not activatable. Account scope mismatches never migrate.

The legacy saved-view schema remains readable for host-rendered v1 collections. New integrations use data inputs/data views. Legacy global view operations require all affected surfaces and explicit data permissions; retaining the schema does not restore the removed SDK shell.

# Overrides, identities and maintenance

## File ownership

| File                               | Owner                       | Behavior                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| personalize/config.ts              | Developer                   | Created once; never overwritten or removed by refresh/remove                                             |
| personalize/overrides.json         | Developer                   | Created once; CLI selection flags explicitly merge requested decisions                                   |
| personalize/bindings.lock.json     | Installer                   | Stable IDs and previous selectors; retained on removal; commit this file                                 |
| personalize/capabilities.json      | Installer                   | Client v2 registry generated from discovery plus overrides                                               |
| personalize/server-manifest.json   | Installer                   | Matching backend registry; deploy with planner                                                           |
| personalize/discovery.json         | Installer                   | Versioned discovery/review evidence and reachable workspace files                                        |
| personalize/sources.ts             | Installer                   | Data adapter bindings                                                                                    |
| personalize/components.tsx         | Installer                   | Host data-input/children adapters (explicit legacy items supported)                                      |
| personalize/navigation.ts          | Installer                   | Approved destination closures                                                                            |
| personalize/root.tsx               | Installer                   | Provider-only integration and custom binding merge                                                       |
| .customitin/ownership.json         | Installer                   | Generated hashes, reversible host bindings and unwrapped host snapshots                                  |
| Root and selected screen TSX files | Developer with SDK wrappers | Host code stays editable; only recognized SDK imports/props/wrappers are maintained                      |
| package.json scripts               | Shared                      | Only selected script wrappers/helper entries are maintained; other package fields remain developer-owned |

Do not edit installer-owned files to customize behavior. Change overrides or supply runtime bindings through config.ts, then refresh. Existing generated-file edits block replacement/removal rather than being silently discarded. Developer config, overrides and the identity lock remain on removal. Retaining the lock keeps moved/renamed selector overrides usable if the integration is installed again.

Edit selected screens and the app root normally: JSX content, props, styles, hooks, callbacks, imports and surrounding providers belong to the developer. Generated screens keep ordinary nested JSX inside CustomizableLayout. The CLI supplies a static sectionIds map and adds stable React keys where missing. Keep section keys stable; an added key remains ordinary host code if an edited screen is later removed from the integration.

Discovery and refresh unwrap recognized SDK syntax from the **current** file, retain host edits and regenerate the bindings. Formatting changes are accepted. Removing the integration or disabling a screen strips only SDK instrumentation from the latest source; an unchanged host file is restored byte-for-byte from its unwrapped snapshot. Root edits are preserved too. Removing a section, adding a section, or changing its default order requires regeneration, while content/style/handler changes work immediately through normal Fast Refresh.

Do not hand-edit generated wrapper imports, aliases, IDs or sectionIds. Changes to those boundaries stop refresh/removal with diagnostics and no writes. Restore the indicated SDK syntax; there is no need to remove/reinstall the integration. Ordinary generated adapters under personalize/ retain whole-file drift protection. Never edit ownership hashes to bypass checks. Older installations without reversible host metadata upgrade on a refresh when their tracked host files are unchanged; if already modified, preserve those edits and restore the last generated host version before upgrading, then reapply the edits.

A moved screen is recognized only when its original path is absent and exactly one new file retains its complete SDK wrapper. A unique unchanged export name keeps the existing identity; use an explicit symbol override for renames. Ambiguous copies, splitting/merging instrumented files and modified wrapper aliases need deliberate host wiring or restoring the known SDK boundaries first. No move is inferred from a partial match.

## Complete override example

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sources": {
    "src/data.ts#loadEntries": {
      "enabled": true,
      "completeness": "complete",
      "title": "Entries",
      "fields": ["id", "title", "stage"],
      "idField": "id",
      "titleField": "title",
      "maxRows": 500,
      "detailDestination": "src/app/entries/[id].tsx"
    }
  },
  "components": {
    "src/EntryCard.tsx#EntryCard": {
      "enabled": true,
      "source": "src/data.ts#loadEntries",
      "defaults": {}
    }
  },
  "routes": {
    "src/app/entries/[id].tsx": { "enabled": true, "title": "Entry details" }
  }
}
```

Only use actual discovered selectors. The example is not universally applicable: if EntryCard requires an excluded field such as note, include it or adapt the host card. Defaults must satisfy the component's scalar rules. Use the JSON Schema produced by `customitin schema` as the authoritative list of supported properties.

`enabled: false` disables a discovered capability without changing application code. Disabling a source can make dependent card bindings unavailable; diagnostics report the mismatch. A field allowlist controls what gets projected to SDK collections. It does not change the host repository.

## Stable identity

The lock records a persistent ID, current selector and previous selectors for each discovered capability. On refresh, an exact selector keeps its ID. A unique export name of the same kind moved to another file can also keep its ID. Ambiguous names do not get guessed. Previous selectors remain aliases, so existing override keys still resolve after a file move.

For a rename or an ambiguous move, retain the old override key or stable ID and point `symbol` to the new selector:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sources": {
    "src/data.ts#loadEntries": {
      "symbol": "src/repository.ts#readEntries",
      "title": "Entries"
    }
  }
}
```

Use this only for the same logical capability. Rebinding a source ID to unrelated data can make saved filters misleading. The CLI preserves identity, not business equivalence.

Manifest revisions are derived from capability semantics, excluding evidence file/line locations. Moving an otherwise unchanged source does not obsolete profiles. Changing fields, operators, labels or binding restrictions can change the revision. Deploy the new server manifest and retain older supported revisions. When a field disappears, runtime reconciliation disables incompatible views rather than removing restrictive filters.

Bindings missing from the current scan remain in the lock as identity history. Overrides that refer to missing active bindings produce diagnostics. Update symbol or explicitly disable them. The lock also stores optional installer-AI source selections, so a later refresh without --ai retains the choice.

Pre-lock installations import matching original source IDs when possible. If a legacy source moved or was renamed before the first upgrade refresh, review the old manifest and restore its selector first or perform an explicit reviewed migration. Do not delete the lock to resolve conflicts.

## Development command integration

Init/refresh automatically wraps recognized `start`, `dev`, `web`, `ios` and `android` scripts that directly run `vite`, `expo start`, `react-native start` or `rnc-cli start`. Optional `npx`/`npx --no-install`, `pnpm exec` and `yarn exec` prefixes are recognized. Build/run-ios/run-android scripts and custom environment/launcher prefixes are not inferred. No process-runner dependency is added. Existing installations need one `refresh --apply` with the updated CLI.

For example, an existing `"start": "expo start"` becomes:

```json
{
  "start": "customitin dev --script start --",
  "customitin:host:start": "expo start"
}
```

Developers continue to use `npm start`, including arguments such as `npm start -- --port 8085`. The wrapper runs the saved host command through the invoking package manager, inherits its environment and terminal streams, starts an applying watcher, and shuts down both together. Host exit codes are retained; SIGINT/SIGTERM stop the host process tree. Existing pre/post hooks remain on the original script and run according to the package manager's normal rules. The host command's `npm_lifecycle_event` is the helper name; scripts that inspect it need adjustment or opt-out.

To select a custom development script, or an exact set of scripts, use repeatable flags:

```sh
npx --no-install customitin refresh --dev-script develop --apply
```

This persists `"devScripts": ["develop"]` in overrides. Only those names are wired when an explicit list is present. `--no-dev-watch` persists `"devScripts": false`, restores current host commands and disables automatic wiring. Remove that override to return to automatic detection. Lifecycle hooks and scripts already running Customitin dev/watch cannot be selected.

Edit `customitin:host:<name>` when changing a wrapped command's flags or launcher. The current helper value is preserved through refresh and restored to the original script on opt-out/removal. Unrelated package fields/scripts are preserved. Missing/modified wrappers and conflicting reserved helper or helper lifecycle names block writes with diagnostics; restore the recorded boundary before retrying. Package formatting may normalize when script entries change. Do not edit ownership metadata to bypass a conflict.

Nested wrapped scripts share their parent watcher. Separate development commands for the same real app directory elect one applying watcher through a temporary OS-directory lock; another command can take over when its owner exits. An additional standalone applying watcher reports a conflict. Dead process locks are recovered automatically. Stop development processes before one-shot applying init/refresh/remove commands. Dry-run watchers do not acquire a writer lock.

Only invoking the development command executes host scripts. Init, refresh, inspect, doctor and standalone watch retain static discovery. The real process tests cover npm on macOS; verify interactive Metro/Expo shortcuts, shutdown and argument forwarding on other package managers and operating systems before claiming support for them.

## Refresh workflow

Normally, use the app's wired development command. For an opted-out or externally managed dev server, the standalone command remains available:

```sh
npx --no-install customitin watch --apply
```

Watch requires an installed integration. It polls bounded source files, overrides, config and tracked output once per second, serializes regeneration and reports changed files or actionable issues as JSON lines. It never runs host scripts or invokes installer AI. Without --apply it only reports plans; --dry-run takes precedence. Stop with Ctrl+C. Edits arriving during planning cause that plan to be skipped and retried on a later poll. Unsupported JSX or altered SDK boundaries keep the last generated integration intact; save a supported correction and watch resumes. Newly added/removed sections show the host container without customization controls while registration is stale, so a save does not hide new UI or throw a section mismatch error. Structural changes can remount sections during this development transition.

Watch is optional. A one-shot workflow is also supported:

1. Update the host code directly; keep section keys stable.
2. Run inspect; compare actual signatures and fields.
3. Update only overrides/config as needed.
4. Run refresh --dry-run and review changed files, unresolved items and conflicts.
5. Apply the same plan with refresh --apply.
6. Run doctor --typecheck and the host's lint/tests/bundles.
7. Exercise a previously saved profile and any changed data/navigation behavior.
8. Deploy matching backend manifests before requiring them in a new app build.

Before a release, stop development commands, run refresh --apply, doctor --typecheck and the app's checks even if watch was running. Review and commit source/generated changes together, including package.json, .customitin/ownership.json and bindings.lock.json. Deploy matching server manifests when capability semantics change. Do not run one-shot applying CLI operations concurrently with an applying watcher.

## What refresh does not do

It does not run application modules, silently change credentials, upgrade frameworks, infer tenant restrictions, merge arbitrary custom code, migrate all existing styles, deploy a backend, or publish a mobile release. These remain explicit host implementation/release tasks.

## Generated formatting

The CLI formats generated TypeScript and the root wrapper before recording ownership hashes. It reads portable literal settings from JSON prettier files, package.json.prettier, and simple module.exports/export-default object configs. It never executes a host configuration or loads formatter plugins. Dynamic configs, YAML, overrides and custom plugins fall back to portable defaults; these are not a promise to reproduce every host formatting rule. To change generated output, adjust a supported static config and refresh before running a formatter over installer-owned files. Check TypeScript files explicitly: the default bare React Native lint script may only scan JavaScript unless `--ext .js,.jsx,.ts,.tsx` is supplied.

## Reviewed enablement and v2 migration

`inspect` prints a readable report; `inspect --json` contains the exact `review.digest`. `init/refresh --approve-report DIGEST --exclude ID_OR_SELECTOR` approves the suggested compatible set against that snapshot. The CLI persists explicit enabled stable IDs. New components/sources discovered by watch stay pending. Completeness annotations do not enable sources, and component annotations do not bypass report review. Required callback/complex-prop candidates remain reported with adapter work; they do not block unrelated unselected bindings.

Workspace discovery follows reachable local files, including compiler-resolved aliases and re-exports. Watch hashes those files as well as app sources. Changing an existing source's shape can change its capability revision; surface field allowlists still control access. Review semantic changes and deploy matching manifests. Source moves retain identity only under the existing unambiguous rules; no identity implies authorization for a new logical dataset.

The alpha SDK now exports headless APIs. Existing config/overrides remain developer-owned during installer migration. Refresh replaces tracked generated files only after ownership checks. The old shell, editors and theme primitives live in examples; update host imports deliberately if the app chose to use them. Installation no longer inserts routes, tabs, appearance tokens or controls. Plan/inspect the migration before applying it, then supply host UI and surface policies.

V2 profile storage uses separate keys. Migration preserves compatible host components by stable ID and reports unsupported shell/theme/navigation settings. It never overwrites v1 bytes. V2 writes and erasure record a retirement marker to prevent automatic v1 fallback after the user resets their retained configuration. Recovery from old bytes is a separate deliberate host workflow, with scope verification. Do not remove those bytes as a side effect of SDK installation. Legacy configuration/identity-lock file formats remain version 1 for ownership compatibility; runtime manifests/profiles/reports are version 2.


---

<!-- Source: docs/ai/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                                 | Check and fix                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Nothing new appears after install                       | Expected: the SDK is headless. Place a host-owned surface and controls; enable approved components/sources.                                                                    |
| Discovered component is not enabled                     | Review `inspect`, approve its current digest or explicitly select it. Refresh keeps new candidates pending.                                                                    |
| Required callback/complex prop                          | Supply a wrapper with declared data inputs/events that calls existing host services. Do not cast away the requirement or infer callback behavior.                              |
| Source is incomplete                                    | Confirm semantics only if the entire authorized dataset is available. Otherwise use an explicit remote executor; never mark a cache complete.                                  |
| Approval digest changed                                 | Reinspect current source/config and review the new report; do not reuse an old digest.                                                                                         |
| Missing root or ambiguous routers                       | Place the provider manually under required host providers; select real navigation bindings. Vite gets automatic web setup first.                                               |
| COMPONENT_UNBOUND / SOURCE_UNBOUND / ACTION_UNBOUND     | Connect the reported stable capability ID through runtime bindings. Registration adds no fallback UI.                                                                          |
| SOURCE_DESCRIPTOR_MISMATCH                              | Adapter and client/server manifests must describe the same capability revision and fields. Refresh/deploy matching metadata.                                                   |
| DATA_CARDINALITY                                        | A single-record input received multiple rows. Add a reviewed selector/filter or use a many-record input.                                                                       |
| DATA_FAILED                                             | Inspect plan/type/nullability/source permissions, completeness, budgets and remote response shape. Use the hook's refresh/more commands with host feedback.                    |
| Actions do not execute                                  | Proposals are separate from execution. Supply host confirmation, permissions, arguments, a current revision/account, and an available handler. Preview/apply blocks execution. |
| Action timed out after dispatch                         | Do not automatically retry a mutation. Reconcile with the host service using its durable idempotency record.                                                                   |
| Saved changes rejected                                  | Reconcile capability revisions and stable IDs. Unsupported v1 shell/theme settings are reported; original v1 bytes remain recoverable.                                         |
| Generated file drift                                    | Preserve edits, move intended changes into config/overrides, then restore the tracked generated boundary before refresh/removal.                                               |
| Local section disappears or remounts during development | Keep keys stable; refresh static registration after structural edits. While stale, the wrapper shows the current host container. Check native geometry/device behavior.        |
| Web tries to load React Native                          | Import shared APIs from `@customitin/react`, DOM integration from `/dom`, and browser storage from `/storage`. Do not import the native example UI into a web-only app.        |

Inspect runtime codes and registration diagnostics in developer-owned tooling. Avoid exposing internal adapter errors, records, credentials or raw service responses to end users or the model. `doctor --typecheck` supplies static evidence only; test the host interaction and deployment separately.

<!-- Source: docs/ai/testing.md -->

# Verification and release checks

Run from the repository:

```sh
npm run docs:build
npm run check
npm run test:consumer
npm run test:e2e
npm run build -w @customitin/web-example
npm run bundle:ios -w @customitin/task-example
npm run bundle:android -w @customitin/task-example
```

`check` includes strict TypeScript, zero-warning lint, formatting, unit/interaction/installer tests, all five package builds, platform/domain boundaries and documentation freshness. The process-tree tests send SIGINT to their own children; a restricted sandbox may deny process-group signalling. Run that verification in an environment permitting owned-child cleanup rather than suppressing the assertion.

`test:consumer` packs local packages and installs isolated native and Vite fixtures without workspace SDK aliases. It follows separate runtime/development installs, exercises Vite's referenced app tsconfig and aliased named chart interface, verifies no-write dry runs, digest approval/exclusions, stale approval rejection and pending discoveries, and checks provider-only install/doctor/idempotency/reversible removal. It then uses the actual generated provider, adapters and source loaders to preview/discard/apply one existing chart with two datasets (`team`/`hours` and `department`/`budget`), reload saved layout and undo. The chart stays unrestricted to a single source; mappings are explicit.

These packed interactions run in jsdom with React DOM; the native harness substitutes React Native Web and in-memory AsyncStorage only for that interaction check. Separate iOS/Android Metro bundles use the real native packages, and Vite runs its TypeScript build and production bundle. This is JavaScript integration evidence, not a native-device launch. The runner prints its temporary evidence directory, including commands/reports, interaction logs and bundle logs. Peer/test packages are installed from the npm cache with `--offline`; seed the cache normally first if required. It does not generate signed native binaries or publish packages. The older official-template fixture under `fixtures/fresh-react-native` is historical and is not the v2 acceptance runner.

The runner also renders each generated existing-screen integration from installed packages and exercises its original callback. Native import/require identity checks and both Metro source maps verify that the shared provider/hooks use one module instance. Source aliases or successful compilation alone would miss duplicate-context failures at package entry points.

## Native simulator pilot

`fixtures/native-pilot/README.md` describes a separate official React Native 0.83.10 app created with the community CLI and installed from packed SDK artifacts. Run `node scripts/consumer/pilot.mjs /path/to/fresh/app` after installing its dependencies. The setup reviews the fixture's capabilities, generates its integration, configures real AsyncStorage and checks strict TypeScript. Build a Release simulator app with embedded JavaScript for actual terminate/relaunch persistence checks.

This pilot covers general UI customization: a reusable chart with two source mappings, summary cards, nested panel/text composition, a host wrapper around a native slider library, a property-only heading, and existing keyed input/callback sections. Its controls and keyboard/safe-area layout are host code. Use its documented checklist for preview/discard/apply, process-restart persistence, undo, reorder/hide, mounted form state, keyboard visibility and rotation. A deterministic planner isolates SDK behavior; it does not validate a live model.

Browser tests use developer-owned controls: the Vite workspace and task-app native workspace exercise chart/table data recombination, preview/discard/apply, layout persistence/undo, and explicit action confirmation. Existing examples exercise legacy host-owned controls. Playwright starts local dev servers; install a browser in the normal host environment or set `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE` to an available browser executable.

## Acceptance evidence

- Installer tests compare provider-only output and unchanged host styles/navigation; unsupported unselected candidates do not block valid ones. Compiling fixtures cover array/record props, memo, children, shared imports/re-exports and DOM/native sections.
- Surface interactions preserve keyed local inputs/callbacks through reordering/hiding/cancel/apply and profile reload. Host state persistence across a process restart is not supplied by the SDK.
- Core/server tests reject unavailable components, fields/actions, cross-surface mutations, missing targets, stale revisions and account changes.
- Data tests cover joins/nulls/type mismatch/incomplete sources, budgets, cancellation, remote result validation and invalidation. Adapters must independently prove full authorized dataset semantics.
- Action tests cover explicit confirmation, preview/save exclusion, duplicate IDs, failures, no automatic retry, account cancellation and backend revalidation/idempotency hooks. Tests use deterministic adapters, not live business mutations.
- Storage tests cover atomic writes/recovery, v1 byte preservation, compatible migration, unsupported appearance settings and prevention of v1 resurrection after erasure.

## Required host and release work

Choose surface placement and all user-facing UI. Review provider context and source completeness. Implement adapter exceptions, stable record IDs, account scope/storage, backend authorization, remote aggregation/pagination where necessary, action confirmation and durable idempotency. Deploy the matching manifest before requiring its revision in a client build.

Check real native devices, navigation/provider geometry, screen-reader focus and hidden content, keyboard/text scaling, performance on realistic data, offline/online transitions and account switching. Measure bundle/startup/frame/memory behavior rather than inferring it from unit tests. Validate live-model clarification, reliability, prompt injection, costs and recovery against the host's actual policies. Signed binaries, accessibility, performance, independent developer pilots and live-model validation remain explicit release gates. A passing automated suite does not establish them.

<!-- Source: docs/ai/cli-reference.md -->

# CLI reference

Commands operate in the current app or `--cwd /absolute/path`. Default mutations are dry runs; `--apply` writes and `--dry-run` takes precedence. Source analysis never executes host modules/scripts. Only `dev` launches the requested host development command.

| Command/flag                                           | Behavior                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inspect`                                              | Readable v2 report, suggested bindings, attention items and approval digest                                  |
| `inspect --json`                                       | Versioned source inventory and `review` (including `review.digest`)                                          |
| `inspect --context`                                    | Exact optional installer-model context and separate `contextDigest`                                          |
| `init`, `refresh`                                      | Provider/binding plan; neither adds visual UI/navigation/theme                                               |
| `--approve-report DIGEST`                              | Enable the reviewed suggested set; stale reports fail                                                        |
| `--exclude ID_OR_SELECTOR`                             | Repeatable exclusions from that reviewed set                                                                 |
| `--complete SELECTOR`                                  | Enable a source and explicitly confirm completeness                                                          |
| `--component SELECTOR`                                 | Explicitly enable a reusable host component                                                                  |
| `--screen SELECTOR`                                    | Instrument static existing sections, retaining their host scope                                              |
| `--route SELECTOR`                                     | Register a navigation binding; adds no route or tab                                                          |
| `--detail SOURCE=ROUTE`                                | Explicit legacy item-detail binding                                                                          |
| `--query-client SELECTOR`, `--navigation-ref SELECTOR` | Choose existing exported host instances                                                                      |
| `doctor --typecheck`                                   | Ownership, package, manifest and static TypeScript checks; not runtime/device verification                   |
| `watch --apply`                                        | Refresh an installed integration without enabling new discoveries                                            |
| `dev --script NAME -- ARGS`                            | Run the saved host command and one shared applying watcher                                                   |
| `--dev-script NAME`, `--no-dev-watch`                  | Persist script selection/opt-out while preserving host commands                                              |
| `remove --apply`                                       | Remove tracked SDK instrumentation while preserving current host code, config, overrides and IDs             |
| `schema`                                               | Authoritative JSON schema for developer-owned overrides                                                      |
| `guide --topic TOPIC`                                  | Print packaged AI guide: index, integration, contracts, maintenance, troubleshooting, testing, cli-reference |

Enablement is independent from the optional installer model. `--ai --approve-context DIGEST` requires `CUSTOMITIN_INSTALLER_API_KEY` and `CUSTOMITIN_INSTALLER_MODEL`, sends only the separately reviewed bounded context, and can choose known supported source adapters. It cannot invent bindings, infer authorization/completeness or bypass manifest validation. Runtime personalization uses the developer's authenticated planner endpoint instead.

Use stable IDs and actual selectors from the report. Review exclusions and source field permissions before approving. Generated `personalize/discovery.json` records evidence; executable adapters stay in TypeScript. Exit code 1 indicates actionable issues/conflicts. Preserve generated drift for review; do not rewrite ownership hashes.
